notes: Real commands against an isolated lease domain (so the benchmark cannot queue behind or block other agents). Foreground = verify-before-push.sh --regular (regular suite + production build); background = run-test-suite.sh full on tests/systems (+ the hook suite); AI-long = run-ai-long-horizon.sh on a miniature of the long-horizon matrix (lh-standard-medium, lh-veteran-medium and the determinism tests -- the two-file shape that fileParallelism acts on); focused = one vitest file.

Scenario 10 ran twice. Run 1 (kept here) has valid timings; its recorded failed check was a defect in the harness (foreground was timed from a job that was itself still queued) and was fixed. Run 2 is an observation, not a pass: another agent was running a full suite in the real lease domain, so four heavyweight jobs ran at once (above the scheduler design ceiling of three) and the foreground job hit the former fixed 600s test ceiling.
The hook suite (which the full/regular jobs run) includes a short synthetic burn of this harness itself; it adds a few seconds of CPU to those jobs.
